angles.name: The Soft Lie Angle
angles.core_idea: Trying harder with pads that flatten is not control — it's a loop.
angles.headline: I kept buying gel pads that went flat.
angles.hollow: The drawer is full of dead cushions. Each one felt like diligence for a few days. Then the pancake returned and so did the hobble — effort with nothing to show.
angles.villain: Compressible drugstore gel and foam pads that collapse under real load.
angles.dream: Foot slides into the shoe and meets a firm arch answer — shape, not mush.
angles.story_arc: I bought the soft pad. Relief. Flat. Buy again. I called it a plan. The twist: softness was the trap. I needed structure under the arch, not another temporary cloud.
angles.product_fit: StrideForm's contoured arch and heel cushion redistribute pressure instead of compressing into another soft lie.

angles.name: The Smaller Life Angle
angles.core_idea: Waiting doesn't pause what heel pain steals — it schedules a smaller life.
angles.headline: I scheduled a future without morning runs.
angles.hollow: The training calendar becomes a museum. You stop arguing with next month and start editing your life down to what a stabbed heel allows.
angles.villain: Wait-and-stretch-only advice that never changes how the foot lands.
angles.dream: Laces pulled tight without bargaining with a future version of yourself who quit.
angles.story_arc: I said it was temporary. Skipped runs stacked up. Stretching bought time that wasn't time. The twist: waiting was the whole plan — and it was shrinking me. I needed today's load to change.
angles.product_fit: A structured orthotic contour changes landing geometry now — a door back to mornings before the smaller life hardens.

angles.name: The Flat Gel Angle
angles.core_idea: The pad you trusted to protect the heel may be what quit on you.
angles.headline: The gel pad went flat and took my mornings.
angles.hollow: You believed the soft cushion was care. When it died midweek, mornings felt like betrayal with a receipt from the pharmacy aisle.
angles.villain: Drugstore gel heel pads that flatten into a hard nothing.
angles.dream: Open the shoe weeks later and still see contour — something that kept its shape.
angles.story_arc: The gel felt kind. I trusted it. Then it pancaked and the stab came home. The twist wasn't that I was dramatic — the helper failed. I stopped needing softer. I needed something that wouldn't quit.
angles.product_fit: StrideForm's non-collapsing arch contour is built to resist the pancake failure mode that burned trust.

angles.name: The Bench Parent Angle
angles.core_idea: Heel pain doesn't just stop runs — it rewrites who you think you are.
angles.headline: I became the bench parent on purpose.
angles.hollow: You choose the bench before anyone asks. Runner, chaser, play person — those labels feel like costumes from another season.
angles.villain: The "just getting older" cope that turns hobbling into a personality.
angles.dream: Mid-chase laughter without narrating the limp to yourself.
angles.story_arc: I used to play until the whistle. Then I sat out and called it maturity. The twist: it wasn't a new identity. It was a hostile landing wearing my face. I needed the foot supported, not a new story about who I'd become.
angles.product_fit: Pressure redistribution through a contoured insert opens the door back toward the person who could stay in the game.

angles.name: The Snapped Morning Angle
angles.core_idea: Feeling cruel for sitting out means the morning ritual is wrong — not that you are.
angles.headline: I snapped when they asked me to play.
angles.hollow: The ask is innocent. Your heel has already voted. Sharp words arrive before you mean them; guilt stays after they run off without you.
angles.villain: The first-step stab ritual that makes saying yes feel like self-harm.
angles.dream: Tag in the yard — yes — without calculating the heel cost.
angles.story_arc: I wanted to be fun. Instead I barked and sat. I blamed my temper. The twist: the guilt was aimed at me when it belonged to a morning that started with a knife in the heel. Change the landing; the shame has less room.
angles.product_fit: Kinder first-step geometry from structured support reduces the spill of heel rage into parenting.

angles.name: The Stretch Fog Angle
angles.core_idea: You can't be a capable problem-solver if every tip ignores how you land.
angles.headline: Everyone had a stretch; nobody fixed my landing.
angles.hollow: Threads, videos, "just rest." Competence turns into guessing. Ambiguity feels worse than a hard, clear answer under the foot.
angles.villain: Just-stretch / just-rest advice lines with no underfoot structure.
angles.dream: Standing up knowing what you're standing on — a visible, physical answer in the shoe.
angles.story_arc: I followed the tips. Still stabbed. More tips. The twist: I didn't need another slogan. I needed a load answer. Once the arch had a contour job, judgment came back.
angles.product_fit: StrideForm states a clear mechanism — redistribute plantar pressure — so authority returns with a why.

angles.name: The Hallway Limp Angle
angles.core_idea: The limp isn't just pain — it's a competence costume you didn't choose.
angles.headline: I timed hallway walks so nobody saw me limp.
angles.hollow: You map routes and pause behind doors. Public floors become stages. The hobble feels like a verdict on how put-together you are.
angles.villain: Flat fashion sneakers treated as "fine for work" with zero support.
angles.dream: Crossing the open-plan floor without timing your steps between desks.
angles.story_arc: I joked about being stiff. I timed the hallway. I parked far to hide the walk. The twist: my shoe had no structure — the audience wasn't the enemy. Support in the shoes I already wear was the missing piece.
angles.product_fit: StrideForm inserts into daily shoes so public walking stops being a performance of pain.

angles.name: The Unequal Walk Angle
angles.core_idea: When one heel owns the morning, the partnership becomes a rota.
angles.headline: My heel turned us into unequal walking partners.
angles.hollow: Dog walks, school runs, errands slide to them. You say thank you and mean sorry. Tenderness thins into logistics.
angles.villain: Unfinished heel mornings that dump movement chores onto one partner.
angles.dream: Same sidewalk. Shared pace. No apology speech for the limp.
angles.story_arc: We used to walk together. Then I sat out and they carried it. Quiet scorekeeping started. The twist: it wasn't love failing — it was a load imbalance. Fix the morning landing and the rota can loosen.
angles.product_fit: Stable underfoot mornings make shared walks possible again — StrideForm as the door, not the romance fix.
